F-01.description: M2 admin bootstrap falls back to a hard-coded default password for admin@railsense.lk when ADMIN_INITIAL_PASSWORD / ADMIN_PASSWORD are unset. On the tested deployment the default was still valid (one attempt, 200 + admin JWT).
F-01.root_cause: M2-operations-agent/admin/admin_db.py:444-445; no forced change on first login.
F-01.impact: C/I/A High: full M2 admin scope (officer management, model retrain/rollback, incident approval, audit read). Accountability: actions would be attributed to the legitimate admin identity.
F-01.likelihood_just: High: the value is in source and one request suffices.
F-01.severity_just: High. A CVSS 3.1 base score for an Internet-facing system would be 9.8; rated High here because the console is LAN-only in this deployment and M2 admin has no path to safety state (train flags live in M4 behind separate auth). Would be Critical if Internet-exposed.

mitigation.immediate: Rotate the admin password on the shared DB; set ADMIN_INITIAL_PASSWORD everywhere.
mitigation.long_term: Remove the literal default (fail closed), one-time random bootstrap secret, forced first-login change, login lockout and alerting.
mitigation.example_control: os.environ['ADMIN_INITIAL_PASSWORD'] required at bootstrap + must_change_password flag
mitigation.retest: Documented default returns 401; bootstrap without env var refuses to start.

F-01.viva_sev: Zero-skill full admin = High; not Critical only because LAN-only and no safety-state path.
F-01.viva_mit: Fail-closed bootstrap secret + forced first-login change.

F-02.description: M4 engineer accounts are a source-code dict with plaintext, weak passwords compared with ==. The documented admin account logged in (200, token issued); a wrong password returned 401.
F-02.impact: Integrity/safety High: the engineer role controls train maintenance flags, which gate ticket sales in M3, and field reports.
F-02.likelihood_just: High: credentials are in the repository and follow a guessable pattern.
F-02.severity_just: High: grants the only safety-relevant write role. Not Critical because the authentication gate itself works (401 without token on all surfaces) and flag changes are visible and reversible.

mitigation.immediate: Change all four passwords via env/DB; remove them from source.
mitigation.long_term: Move engineers to the DB with bcrypt (reuse M2's officer model), per-user accounts, lockout, MFA for flagging.
mitigation.example_control: bcrypt.checkpw against engineers table; secrets loaded from env
mitigation.retest: Source contains no passwords; documented credentials return 401.

F-02.viva_sev: Public credentials for the safety-relevant role = High.
F-02.viva_mit: Hashed DB-backed engineer accounts; no secrets in source.

F-03.description: Gateway admin and monitor routes proxy to Booking/Hub with no session check. Without a token, on both :3000 (public) and :3001: fraud-reviews (17 cases incl. names, emails, risk scores), cancellations, hub dashboard/timeline; system-health and admin/trains on :3000. Booking /internal/fraud-reviews is also unauthenticated.
F-03.impact: Confidentiality High: passenger PII and AI fraud-risk labels disclosed; internal topology (base URLs) disclosed. RAI: exposes who was flagged as a fraud risk by an automated model.
F-03.likelihood_just: High on the LAN: public port bound to 0.0.0.0, plain GET, no auth.
F-03.severity_just: High: unauthenticated read of personal data plus automated risk judgements. Not Critical because the routes are read-only (review actions were not tested and M2's admin API behind the same gateway correctly returns 401).

mitigation.immediate: Require an officer session on every /api/admin/* and /api/hub/* gateway route; stop serving admin routes on :3000.
mitigation.long_term: Central auth middleware at the gateway plus independent auth in Booking/Security admin routes.
mitigation.example_control: FastAPI dependency verifying the M2 officer JWT + role claim on an APIRouter prefix
mitigation.retest: All listed routes return 401 for none/passenger and 403 for operator where admin-only.

F-03.viva_sev: Unauthenticated PII + fraud labels on a LAN-facing port = High.
F-03.viva_mit: Gateway-level auth dependency on the admin/hub router prefix.

F-16.description: In 4 of 17 fraud cases (8 of 21 passenger objects) booking_details.passengers[] contains a raw 12-digit nic next to nic_masked and nic_hash; last 4 digits match the mask in 8/8. Served unauthenticated via F-03. Corrects the Stage-1 conclusion that NIC masking fully held.
F-16.root_cause: booking-agent/fraud/review_service.py:99 copies caller payload incl. passengers[].nic into booking_payload; list_cases (review_service.py:40-62) returns it verbatim. Current booking path (booking/service.py:283-291, 379) is sanitised, so the exposure is legacy rows / the helper path.
F-16.impact: Confidentiality High: national identity numbers are a durable identifier used for identity verification. Data protection: contradicts the README's HMAC/mask claim. Whether values are synthetic could not be determined; treated as PII.
F-16.likelihood_just: High: reachable through the unauthenticated F-03 route.
F-16.severity_just: High on its own (national ID disclosure); combined with F-03 it is the most sensitive exposure found. Not Critical because it affects 4 historical cases, not every booking.

mitigation.immediate: Scrub nic from stored booking_payload rows (one-off migration); fix F-03.
mitigation.long_term: Strip raw identifiers in create_review_case and apply a response-side allowlist in list_cases; add a regression test that no response contains a raw NIC pattern.
mitigation.example_control: p.pop('nic', None) before persisting; serializer allowlist {name, nic_masked, nic_hash}
mitigation.retest: Scan of fraud-reviews finds 0 raw NIC values; unit test for create_review_case.

F-16.viva_sev: National ID disclosure = High; limited to 4 legacy cases, so not Critical.
F-16.viva_mit: Scrub at write, allowlist at read, migrate old rows.

F-04.description: M2, M4, Security, Booking and Hub use allow_origins=['*'] with allow_credentials=True, so Starlette reflects any Origin with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. M1 returns ACAO * without credentials.
F-04.root_cause: M2 main.py:100-101; agent-hub/main.py:121-122; booking-agent/main.py:109-110; M4 main.py:254-255; security-agent/main.py:46-47.
F-04.impact: Medium: tokens are Bearer headers from localStorage (not cookies), so credentialed CORS does not currently leak sessions. The permissive origin policy still lets any web page a staff member opens read unauthenticated loopback-only services from their browser, weakening the 127.0.0.1 bind. Becomes High if cookie auth is introduced.
F-04.likelihood_just: Medium: requires a victim to visit an attacker page while on the host.
F-04.severity_just: Medium: a real misconfiguration with a cross-origin read path, but session theft is not possible with the current token storage.

mitigation.immediate: Replace '*' with the two gateway origins; drop allow_credentials where unused.
mitigation.long_term: Shared CORS config module; internal services need no browser CORS at all.
mitigation.retest: Preflight with Origin https://evil.example returns no ACAO header.

F-04.viva_sev: Medium: reflection is real, but Bearer-in-header tokens are not sent automatically.
F-04.viva_mit: Explicit origin allowlist; never * with credentials.

F-05.description: Receivers do not verify the Hub delegation token. Security /internal/fraud-score answered 200 with no token; other internal endpoints reached schema validation (422) with no auth check; M4 /hub/message accepted no-token and wrong-key tokens (200).
F-05.root_cause: security-agent/main.py:99-105 (no auth dependency); M4 main.py:120-122 (_verify_hub_token returns when JWT_SECRET_KEY unset = fail-open).
F-05.impact: Integrity Medium: bypasses the Hub's signature, allowlist, rate limit and audit for anyone who can reach a receiver (localhost, gateway pass-through, or SSRF).
F-05.likelihood_just: Medium: internal ports are loopback, but the gateway proxies /svc/* on 0.0.0.0.
F-05.severity_just: Medium: a defence-in-depth failure that needs a network precondition; no direct PII or safety write was demonstrated through it.

mitigation.immediate: Set JWT_SECRET_KEY in M4 and make verification fail closed.
mitigation.long_term: Shared verify_agent_token dependency on every /internal/* and /hub/message route; mTLS or per-agent keys.
mitigation.location: security-agent/main.py:99; M4 main.py:114-133; booking/M2 internal routes
mitigation.retest: No-token and wrong-key calls to all receivers return 401.

F-05.viva_sev: Medium: needs network reach; it removes a layer rather than exposing data by itself.
F-05.viva_mit: Fail-closed token verification at every receiver.

F-06.description: Both gateways listen on 0.0.0.0 (confirmed by netstat); internal agents listen on 127.0.0.1. The gateway re-exposes admin, hub and /svc/* routes to the LAN.
F-06.impact: Medium: amplifier that makes F-03, F-05, F-11 reachable from any device on the network.
F-06.severity_just: Medium: no data exposure on its own; it widens who can reach other weaknesses.

mitigation.long_term: Authenticating reverse proxy/ingress; separate admin plane not exposed to passengers.

F-06.viva_sev: Amplifier, not a direct exposure = Medium.

F-07.description: Independent retrieval results are below README claims: M1 P@1 0.542 (EN 1.000 / SI 0.375 / TA 0.250), M2 0.875 vs claimed 1.000, M4 0.792 vs claimed 1.000. No retriever applies a relevance threshold (off-topic queries return chunks; M4 FP rate 0.5).
F-07.evidence: evidence/S4-M1-01, S4-M2-01, S4-M4-01 results.json; figures/fig_retrieval_metrics.png, fig_language_gap.png
F-07.root_cause: M1 rag/retriever.py:15-26, 38 (English-only MiniLM, unconditional top_k); M2 evaluation/rag/evaluate_retrieval.py:3-4 (corpus-derived queries); M4 manual_retriever.py:133 (TF-IDF, no cutoff) and shipped eval prefixing gold asset/fault type.
F-07.impact: Medium: degraded answers for Sinhala/Tamil passengers (fairness); overstated public metrics (transparency); irrelevant 'authoritative' context for off-topic questions.
F-07.likelihood_just: High: affects ordinary usage by every non-English user.
F-07.severity_just: Medium: a quality/fairness defect, not a security breach; LLM declines in S4-M1-02 limited the harm observed. Risk is High because it occurs in normal use every day.

mitigation.immediate: Publish the independent figures alongside the README numbers.
mitigation.long_term: Multilingual embeddings (e.g. paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2) or translate-then-retrieve; similarity threshold with an 'I don't know' path; held-out multilingual eval set in CI.
mitigation.location: the three retriever modules and eval scripts
mitigation.example_control: if top_distance > tau: return [] (tau tuned on held-out set)
mitigation.retest: Re-run the 24-query sets: SI/TA P@1 within 0.15 of EN; off-topic FP rate < 0.1.

F-07.viva_sev: Quality/fairness, not a breach = Medium severity; High risk because it is constant.
F-07.viva_mit: Multilingual embeddings + relevance threshold + honest held-out eval.

F-12.description: One HS256 JWT_SECRET_KEY signs and verifies both officer/admin tokens and all inter-agent Hub tokens.
F-12.evidence: Code review; gray-box token minting in scripts/_harness.py demonstrates that the secret suffices for both token types.
F-12.impact: High if leaked: any holder can mint an admin officer token and impersonate any agent; no separation of trust domains.
F-12.likelihood_just: Low: requires disclosure of the secret (it is in several .env files).
F-12.severity_just: Medium: design weakness with large blast radius but no direct exploit without a prior leak.

mitigation.immediate: Separate secrets for officer tokens and agent tokens.
mitigation.long_term: RS256/ES256 per-agent key pairs so a compromised agent cannot forge others; key rotation.
mitigation.example_control: OFFICER_JWT_SECRET vs per-agent private keys with the Hub holding only public keys
mitigation.retest: An agent token is rejected by the admin API and vice versa.

F-12.viva_sev: Large blast radius but needs a leak first = Medium.

F-08.description: Unauthenticated incident reports are held as pending and correctly kept off the public map, but the Operations Assistant's incident tool lists pending items with their raw summary text (labelled _pending_), so attacker-written text enters an LLM-facing tool unsanitised. Re-rated from Medium (Stage 1) to Low.
F-08.root_cause: M2 ops_agent_tools.py:184-185 (excludes only rejected), summary copied from raw_text; no provenance sanitisation.
F-08.impact: Low: officer-facing only, status label shown; potential indirect prompt-injection surface when the Gemini path is live (not exercised in this run).
F-08.likelihood_just: Medium: submission is unauthenticated and trivial.
F-08.severity_just: Low: listing the review queue is intended behaviour; the gap is unsanitised untrusted text, and no manipulated answer was observed.

mitigation.immediate: Quote/escape pending text as data in tool output; never include pending rows in LLM context except in the explicit review view.
mitigation.long_term: Provenance labels and trust tiers on every retrieved item; injection-pattern stripping.
mitigation.example_control: {'trust':'unverified','text':<escaped>} with a system rule that unverified text is not instructions
mitigation.retest: Injection marker never appears unquoted in assistant answers.

F-08.viva_sev: Intended queue view with visible label; residual injection surface = Low.
F-08.viva_mit: Trust-tier labels and escaping for unverified text.

F-09.description: No X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, CSP or HSTS on any service; /docs and /openapi.json return 200 on all 8 services including both gateways.
F-09.root_cause: FastAPI defaults (docs enabled, no header middleware) in every main.py.
F-09.impact: Low: clickjacking/MIME-sniffing hardening gap; full API map disclosed.
F-09.viva_mit: Disable docs in prod + header middleware.

F-10.description: M1 /chat has no rate limiter (20/20 accepted); M2 /incident-report has no limiter (10/10 near-duplicates accepted). M2/M4 other routes and the Hub do limit.
F-10.root_cause: No slowapi in M1 backend; M2 main.py:1469 lacks the @limiter decorator present on neighbouring routes.
F-10.impact: Low: LLM cost amplification and review-queue spam.
F-10.severity_just: Low: availability/cost impact under bounded conditions; contradicts README claim.

mitigation.long_term: Gateway-wide per-IP limits; duplicate detection on incident text.

F-11.description: GET /chat/{session_id}/history returns another session's messages to any caller with the UUID, directly and via the public gateway.
F-11.root_cause: M1 main.py:1645 (no ownership check); main.py:136-138 validates format only.
F-11.impact: Medium: conversation content (travel details) disclosed if an ID leaks.
F-11.likelihood_just: Low: UUIDv4 is unguessable; requires leakage.
F-11.severity_just: Low: real IDOR, but only exploitable with a leaked identifier.

mitigation.immediate: Remove history route from the public pass-through.
mitigation.long_term: Bind sessions to a signed cookie or authenticated principal and check ownership.
mitigation.example_control: HMAC-signed session cookie compared to path id
mitigation.retest: Reading session A's history from B's context returns 403.

F-11.viva_sev: IDOR gated by an unguessable ID = Low.
F-11.viva_mit: Ownership check via signed session binding.

F-13.description: delay_alert and maintenance_alert are published to Upstash as plain JSON with no signature; subscribers cannot verify origin.
F-13.impact: Medium: forged alerts could mislead consumers.
F-13.severity_just: Low: design gap behind a credential; not exploited.

mitigation.immediate: Add an HMAC field with a dedicated key.
mitigation.long_term: Verify signature and schema on consume; reject unsigned.
mitigation.retest: Unsigned or tampered event is dropped by subscriber.

F-14.description: M1 accepted a 120 KB chat message; the Hub forwarded a 200 KB payload.
F-14.root_cause: M1 main.py:90-92 (message: str, no max_length); Hub payload is a free-form dict.
F-14.impact: Low: memory and LLM-token cost amplification.

mitigation.immediate: max_length on message; payload size check in Hub.

F-15.description: The M4 engineer assistant answered a passenger-style question with internal asset IDs/health, and emitted numeric limits without a post-generation check against cited manual text (no fabrication was proven).
F-15.root_cause: No role/scope filter on M4 /chat; number guard not applied to safety figures; invented-ID check skipped when M4 is offline from the shared DB.
F-15.impact: Informational: scope creep; residual over-trust risk for safety figures.
F-15.severity_just: Informational: no incorrect safety value was demonstrated; observed figures were consistent with the manual section returned in S4-M4-04.

mitigation.long_term: Verify each emitted number appears in a cited chunk; show citations.
mitigation.example_control: regex numbers in answer ⊆ numbers in retrieved chunks, else fall back to template
mitigation.retest: Passenger question is redirected; unsupported number triggers template.
